newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper slams weak justice system.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper slams weak justice system.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper, likening his country to a hospital ward where all the patients were dying, said on Thursday that 98 percent of all crimes committed in Colombia go unpunished.
Samper also said up to 100 Colombians were dying every day because of endemic political bloodletting.

"The levels of impunity within the justice system, despite all the fiscal and regulatory efforts that have been made, are incredible," he said. "To talk about 98 percent impunity when it comes to justice is like saying the mortality rate in our hospitals amounts to 100 percent of the patients being treated."

Samper spoke at a ceremony at Casa de Narino presidential palace after swearing in Alfonso Gomez Mendez, a veteran lawyer and jurist, as chief prosecutor. Gomez replaces Alfonso Valdivieso, a highly popular anti-drug and corruption fighter who stepped down in May to launch a bid for the presidency.

"No form of insecurity causes more fear and more harm to a society than insecurity about the protection of justice," Samper said. He urged Gomez, who will serve a four-year term as prosecutor-general, to shore up the notoriously weak judicial system so "that justice works, that it functions, and that it arrives on time and everywhere without distinction."
Government officials have said Colombia's high rate of impunity was one of the reasons it ranks among the world's most violent countries.
"We have serious, very serious, human rights problems," Samper said. "One hundred Colombians are loosing their lives every day on account of political violence."
He did not elaborate on the death toll, but 100 killings a day, or a total of 36,500 a year, would be substantially higher than last year's murder rate of 26,642.
